title: Idempotent completeness of the common-stage category
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime
$\ell\neq p$, a scheme $Y$, and an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\Ql$, and let
$\mathcal C_Y=D^b_c(Y,\Qlb)$ be the common-stage coefficient category of
[def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], whose finite stages are the
rationalized categories $D^b_c(Y,E)$ of
[def-weil-rationalization-karoubi]. Then $\mathcal C_Y$ is idempotent
complete, and the canonical functor

$$
 \mathcal C_Y\longrightarrow\Kar(\mathcal C_Y)
$$

into its Karoubi envelope is an exact equivalence.

proof.text: For each finite subextension $L/\Ql$ in the chosen algebraic closure, use [lem-weil-rationalization-idempotent-complete] with the same scheme $Y$ and field $L$. Its statement concerns exactly $D^b_c(Y,L)$ of [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], and gives idempotent completeness. These are the finite stages specified by [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. Thus every actual idempotent in every stage of this common-stage construction has a splitting. No identification with a different integral coefficient model or with a category of formally adjoined retracts is used.

source.place: Proof, opening finite-stage Karoubianity sentence; use the existing same-unit finite-stage statement for precisely these rationalized categories

proof.text: Let $X=(E,K)$ and $e:X\to X$ satisfy $e^2=e$. By [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], write $e=[L,u]$ with $L\supset E$ finite and $u:K\otimes_E L\to K\otimes_E L$. Common-stage composition gives $e^2=[L,u^2]$; the equality of these two classes has a witness at some finite $M\supset L$. Let $H=-\otimes_L M$ and let $a:H(K\otimes_E L)\xrightarrow{\sim}K\otimes_E M$ be the scalar-extension identification in that definition. The transported representative is $w=aH(u)a^{-1}$, while the transported composite is $aH(u^2)a^{-1}=aH(u)a^{-1}aH(u)a^{-1}=w^2$, by the functor law and cancellation. The equality witness therefore says $w^2=w$ in $D^b_c(Y,M)$. This imposes the idempotent equation at $M$, rather than assuming it already holds at the original representative stage $L$.

source.place: Proof, filtered retract-descent sentence: representative and eventual idempotent equation, expanded directly in this common-stage model

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-rationalization-idempotent-complete] at $M$ to $w$ on $V=K\otimes_E M$. There are $S\in D^b_c(Y,M)$ and arrows $i:S\to V$, $p:V\to S$ with $pi=1_S$ and $ip=w$. In the common-stage category of [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], set $B=(M,S)$ and take the classes of these arrows at $M$, using the unit identifications $S\otimes_M M\cong S$. The common-stage composition rule gives $[M,p][M,i]=[M,pi]=1_B$ and $[M,i][M,p]=[M,w]=e$. Hence every idempotent of $\mathcal C_Y$ splits; the object and both arrows of the splitting have the single finite field $M$ of definition.

source.place: Proof, filtered retract-descent sentence: split at the enlarged finite stage and compute both composites of the resulting classes

proof.text: The category $\mathcal C_Y$ is triangulated by [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], hence additive in the sense of [def-weil-triangulated-category]. For the canonical functor $J:\mathcal C_Y\to\Kar(\mathcal C_Y)$ of [def-weil-karoubi-envelope], [lem-weil-karoubi-envelope-fully-faithful] gives full faithfulness. If $Q=(X,e)$ is an envelope object, step 3 gives $S\xrightarrow{i}X\xrightarrow{p}S$ with $pi=1_S$ and $ip=e$. Then $ei=ipi=i$ and $pe=pip=p$, so the morphism condition $u=d u e$ of the envelope makes $i:J(S)\to Q$ and $p:Q\to J(S)$ morphisms there. Their composites are $1_{J(S)}$ and $e=1_Q$. Thus each $Q$ is isomorphic to an object in the image of $J$.

source.place: Proof, canonical full faithfulness and essential surjectivity sentence; explicit envelope isomorphism from the splitting

proof.text: Here is explicit equivalence data, so no separate equivalence criterion is needed. For each $Q=(X,e)$ choose a splitting $(S_Q,i_Q,p_Q)$ from step 3 and set $G(Q)=S_Q$, $G(u:Q\to R)=p_R u i_Q$. The envelope relation in [def-weil-karoubi-envelope] gives $u e=d u e^2=d u e=u$ and $d u=d^2 u e=d u e=u$ for $R=(Y,d)$. Consequently $G(1_Q)=p_Q e i_Q=1_{S_Q}$ and $G(v)G(u)=p_U v i_R p_R u i_Q=p_U v d u i_Q=p_U vu i_Q=G(vu)$. Distributivity in the additive category gives $G(u+v)=p_R(u+v)i_Q=p_Ru i_Q+p_Rv i_Q=G(u)+G(v)$ and $G(0)=0$, so $G$ is additive. The morphisms $i_Q:JG(Q)\to Q$ are a natural isomorphism, with inverse $p_Q$, because $i_R JG(u)=d u i_Q=u i_Q$. For $Q=J(X)$, the two splitting maps give the natural isomorphism $\eta_X=p_{J(X)}:X\to GJ(X)$: naturality follows from $GJ(f)p_{J(X)}=p_{J(Y)}f i_{J(X)}p_{J(X)}=p_{J(Y)}f$. The triangle equations are $i_{J(X)}J(\eta_X)=1_X$ and $G(i_Q)\eta_{G(Q)}=p_Q i_Q i_{J(S_Q)}p_{J(S_Q)}=p_Q i_Q=1_{S_Q}$. These data exhibit $J$ as an equivalence.

source.place: Proof, equivalence conclusion: expand the elementary quasi-inverse, naturality and triangle equations

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-karoubi-envelope-triangulated] to the triangulated common-stage category supplied by [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. It equips $\Kar(\mathcal C_Y)$ with shift $(X,e)[1]=(X[1],e[1])$ and its retract triangulation, and states that the canonical $J$ is exact. Exactness here is the shift-compatible preservation of distinguished triangles defined by [def-weil-triangulated-category]. Together with the equivalence data of step 5, this proves that $J$ is an exact equivalence, while step 3 proves the other asserted clause, idempotent completeness of $\mathcal C_Y$.
